title: RFC 9110: HTTP Semantics
supports: Opened with WebFetch. Published June 2022. Section 9.2.2: idempotent methods have the same intended effect when repeated; PUT, DELETE and safe methods (GET, HEAD, OPTIONS, TRACE) are idempotent.

title: RFC 9457: Problem Details for HTTP APIs
supports: Opened with WebFetch. Published July 2023, obsoletes RFC 7807; application/problem+json with type, status, title, detail, instance and extensions; do not expose implementation details such as stack dumps.

title: The Idempotency-Key HTTP Header Field (draft-ietf-httpapi-idempotency-key-header)
supports: Opened with WebFetch. Revision 08 updated 22 October 2026, an Internet-Draft, not an RFC, expires 25 April 2027; 409 for a concurrent retry, 422 for a reused key with a different payload, 400 for a missing required key; UUID keys recommended.

title: RateLimit header fields for HTTP (draft-ietf-httpapi-ratelimit-headers)
supports: Opened with WebFetch. Revision 11 updated 23 May 2026, an Internet-Draft, not an RFC; defines RateLimit-Policy and RateLimit fields; Retry-After takes precedence when both are present; suggests jitter.

title: OpenAPI Specification (latest)
supports: Opened with WebFetch. Latest version 3.2.1, dated 10 September 2026.

title: OWASP Top 10 API Security Risks - 2023
supports: Opened with WebFetch (owasp.org/API-Security redirects here). The ten 2023 risks from API1 broken object level authorization to API10 unsafe consumption of APIs, with short descriptions of API1, API3, API4, API6 and API10.

title: Idempotent requests
supports: Opened with WebFetch. Idempotency-Key header on POST; saves status and body of the first request once execution begins, including 500s; keys up to 255 characters, prunable after at least 24 hours; parameters compared; V4 UUIDs suggested; no personal data in keys.

title: Stripe blog post on designing predictable APIs with idempotency (title shortened)
supports: Opened with WebFetch. Published 22 February 2017; the full title uses a word on the kit banned-words list, so it is shortened here. Three ways a request can fail; idempotency keys reused on retries; exponential backoff and jitter.

title: Receive Stripe events in your webhook endpoint
supports: Opened with WebFetch. Verify Stripe-Signature on the raw body; return 2xx before complex logic; retries up to three days in live mode, three times over a few hours in a sandbox; duplicates handled by logging event IDs; order not guaranteed; asynchronous queue; default 5-minute timestamp tolerance, do not use zero.

title: Testing
supports: Opened with WebFetch. Sandboxes and test keys; test card numbers and test PaymentMethods; the Stripe Services Agreement prohibits testing in live mode with real payment method details; 3D Secure and decline test cards.

title: Strong Customer Authentication readiness
supports: Opened with WebFetch. SCA in effect from 14 September 2019 under PSD2; affects EEA businesses serving EEA customers with cards; 3D Secure; Checkout and Payment Intents handle it; UK cards saved before 14 September 2021 could use previous authorisation agreements.

title: Model Context Protocol (MCP)
supports: Opened with WebFetch. Official server at mcp.stripe.com; OAuth or agent API keys; from December 2026 full-access secret keys and restricted keys without the Agent tag are not accepted; human confirmation for actions such as refunds; turn on the client's tool approval.

title: FAQ clarifies new SAQ A eligibility criteria for e-commerce merchants
supports: Opened with WebFetch. Published 28 February 2025. Revised SAQ A for PCI DSS v4.0.1 from 1 April 2025 adds a criterion that the site is not susceptible to script attacks; applies to embedded (for example iframe) payment forms, not redirects or full outsourcing.

title: Standard Webhooks specification
supports: Opened with WebFetch. webhook-id, webhook-timestamp and webhook-signature headers; signs id, timestamp and body; HMAC-SHA256 (v1) or ed25519 (v1a); webhook-id as idempotency key; example retry schedule over about 75 hours with backoff and jitter.

title: Best practices for using webhooks
supports: Opened with WebFetch. Use a secret; respond with 2XX within 10 seconds; process asynchronously; redeliver missed deliveries; X-GitHub-Delivery for replay protection, kept on redelivery.

title: Best practices for webhooks
supports: Opened with WebFetch. X-Shopify-Webhook-Id for duplicates; X-Shopify-Triggered-At or updated_at for ordering; X-Shopify-Hmac-Sha256 verification; delivery not always guaranteed, so run reconciliation jobs.

title: Troubleshooting webhooks
supports: Opened with WebFetch. Respond within five seconds; up to eight retries within four hours; after repeated failures the subscription is removed.

title: Transaction Isolation
supports: Opened with WebFetch. PostgreSQL 18 current, 19 in development; Read Committed is the default; Repeatable Read and Serializable transactions can fail with SQLSTATE 40001 and must be retried.

title: Explicit Locking
supports: Opened with WebFetch. Row-level locks including FOR UPDATE; deadlock detection and consistent lock order; ACCESS EXCLUSIVE blocks even SELECT and is taken by many ALTER TABLE forms.

title: INSERT
supports: Opened with WebFetch. ON CONFLICT DO UPDATE guarantees an atomic insert or update even under high concurrency; conflict target required for DO UPDATE; RETURNING.

title: CREATE INDEX
supports: Opened with WebFetch. A normal build blocks writes; CONCURRENTLY does not but cannot run in a transaction block, takes longer and can leave an invalid index to drop or reindex.

title: Timeouts, retries, and backoff with jitter
supports: Opened with WebFetch (aws.amazon.com/builders-library redirects here). Published 5 December 2019. Timeouts from latency percentiles; retries multiply across layers (243x example); retry at one layer; exponential backoff with cap and jitter; token bucket; only retry idempotent calls.

title: Pattern: Transactional outbox
supports: Opened with WebFetch. Write messages to an outbox in the same transaction; a relay publishes them; messages may be published more than once, so consumers must be idempotent.

title: Parallel Change
supports: Opened with WebFetch. Published 13 May 2014. Expand, migrate, contract phases for backward-incompatible changes; applies to database refactoring.

title: Postmortem of database outage of January 31
supports: Opened with WebFetch. Published 10 February 2017. Data directory removed on the primary; about 300 GB deleted; about 18 hours down; about six hours of database changes lost; pg_dump backups failing silently on a version mismatch; failure emails rejected; restore testing added.

title: Managing environments for deployment
supports: Opened with WebFetch. Required reviewers (up to six people or teams), prevent self-review, wait timer, deployment branch rules, environment secrets; private repositories need GitHub Team or Pro.

title: Express@5.0.0 release
supports: Opened with WebFetch. Post dated 15 October 2024. Requires Node.js 18 or newer; rejected promises go to error middleware; path-to-regexp changes remove regex sub-expressions because of ReDoS; deprecated signatures removed.

title: Node.js Releases
supports: Opened with WebFetch. Node 20 end of life; Node 26 the latest LTS; production should use Active or Maintenance LTS lines; annual releases from Node 27.

title: Principles of the GDPR
supports: Opened with WebFetch. Seven principles including data minimisation (adequate, relevant, limited to what is necessary) and storage limitation (shortest time possible, set time limits to erase or review).

title: Model context protocol (MCP)
supports: Opened with WebFetch. Official Supabase MCP server at mcp.supabase.com; read-only mode runs SQL as a read-only user; project scoping; keep manual approval of tool calls on.
